summary: Advance your future-of-work and workforce transformation skills. Learn to redesign jobs, skills, and work models with data-driven tools.
lede: Future of work training helps senior HR, talent, and workforce-planning professionals assess how technology and changing work patterns affect roles and skills. The practical focus is turning that analysis into skills-based workforce plans, using scenarios and workforce analytics, and designing hybrid work models. Learners also practice mapping AI and automation impacts, prioritizing reskilling or redeployment, and setting governance, measures, and a phased transformation roadmap.
audienceIntro: This advanced Future of Work and Workforce Transformation Training is built for senior professionals who already shape how work, skills, and structures evolve in their organizations and who now need a sharper, data-driven approach to workforce transformation.
audience: Future of Work or Workforce Transformation Program
HR Business Partner for technology or digital
modules: Future of Work Context and Workforce Shifts
Strategic Workforce Planning and Scenario Design
Skills Taxonomy and Dynamic Job Architecture
Designing Hybrid Work and Human plus AI Collaboration
Workforce Transformation Governance and Change Leadership
prerequisites: This is an advanced-level course designed for experienced professionals with responsibility for workforce strategy, HR, or enterprise transformation. You should have at least 5 years of experience in HR, organizational development, strategy, or related fields and be comfortable working with workforce data such as headcount reports, skills inventories, or engagement results. Prior exposure to strategic workforce planning, change management, or operating model design is strongly recommended, though you do not need to be a technical data scientist. No coding or programming is required; you will work with configurable templates and mainstream analytics tools rather than writing software. Advanced concepts such as AI-driven workforce analytics, internal talent marketplaces, and skills taxonomies are taught at the level of operational application and hands-on implementation design, not deep technical engineering. You should bring a laptop capable of working with spreadsheet-based tools and cloud collaboration platforms, and where possible, anonymized examples of your organization’s workforce data and current workforce plans to maximize relevance.
